data.narrative:
Oxa is a Series D stage autonomous systems company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, having raised $103M to date. The valuation universe comprises 8 private peers, including Wayve, Waymo, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro; no public comparables exist in this nascent category.

The peer-median method was inapplicable due to insufficient narrow peer data—only one same-stage comparable was identified within Drones & Autonomous, falling short of the three-datapoint threshold needed for reliable triangulation. A broader sector median would introduce unacceptable cross-stage and cross-segment bias. Consequently, analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical of Series D advancement to the $103M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $154M.

The triangulated range centers on $154M median, with a low of $131M (applying conservative assumptions) and a high of $178M (applying optimistic assumptions). This narrow band reflects the single-method constraint rather than robust cross-validation. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.5x stage multiplier for autonomous systems specifically, near-term funding environment tightening, and whether the $103M raised baseline accurately reflects current market clearing values. A more definitive valuation would require either a recent external financing event or access to a materially broader comparable set at adjacent stages.
